name: Kellstrom & Vane Houndstooth Sport Coat
description:
A single-breasted two-button sport coat in a mid-weight wool-linen blend, cut in a classic houndstooth pattern — charcoal and cream, or a more aggressive black and rust. The lapels are notched and slightly wider than current corporate fashion, a deliberate nod to pre-Collapse tailoring traditions. Patch pockets at the hips. The interior is fully lined in a subtle jacquard silk-analog. Kellstrom & Vane is a mid-tier label out of the old Wicker Park district, family-owned for three generations, stubbornly independent.

This coat is the kind of thing you buy when you want to look like you made considered choices. It's not trying to signal wealth — it signals taste, which in Tier 3 circles is considered more sophisticated. It pairs easily with dark denim or trousers. Academics, junior architects, and mid-level creatives wear it to meetings where they need to be taken seriously without looking like they sold out.
what_it_says: You know what a half-canvas construction is and you care. You're not chasing trends. You have opinions about fabric.
worn_by: Tier 3 professionals who reject corporate fashion
story_hooks: Kellstrom & Vane's third-generation owner has been quietly refusing a buyout offer from Vantablack's lifestyle division for two years — and the pressure is getting less quiet.
A particular run of the rust colorway was commissioned by a Tier 3 political organizing group as informal semi-uniform — subtle enough to be deniable, visible enough to mark allies in a crowd.
The current head tailor, an elderly woman named Priya Solberg, is rumored to sew micro-notes into the lining seams of coats for clients she trusts — old-fashioned dead-drop tradecraft.

physical_description.visual_profile: A structured, slightly oversized single-breasted sport coat with a refined silhouette that reads as intentionally vintage-inspired rather than contemporary corporate. The wider notched lapels and classic cut evoke pre-Collapse tailoring, grounding it in a sense of continuity and craft rather than cutting-edge design. On a body, it drapes with quiet confidence—not aggressively fitted, but not slouchy either.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed-tailored. Sits naturally on the shoulders with room through the chest and torso. Sleeves end just at the wrist bone. Allows for layering underneath without pulling or bunching. Cut to complement a range of body types without drawing attention to silhouette.
physical_description.primary_material: Mid-weight wool-linen blend—durable and breathable, with a slight textural variance that prevents flatness. The blend resists wrinkles while maintaining a lived-in appearance.
physical_description.texture: Subtle houndstooth weave visible on close inspection, creating visual depth without overwhelming. The surface is smooth but not glossy; it has a matte, natural quality. The interior lining is a fine jacquard silk-analog with a soft hand.
physical_description.color_scheme: Two signature options: charcoal base with cream houndstooth (sophisticated, conservative, pairs with everything), or black base with rust/copper houndstooth (more distinctive, slightly avant-garde while remaining grounded). Both read as intentional color choices rather than defaults.
physical_description.closures: Two-button front closure, mother-of-pearl or bone buttons with a subtle satin finish. Clean, understated, functional.
distinctive_features: Notched lapels cut slightly wider than current Tier 2 corpo fashion
Patch pockets at hips—functional and visible, rejecting hidden pocket aesthetic
Full interior jacquard silk-analog lining with subtle geometric or heritage pattern
Subtle Kellstrom & Vane label at interior breast pocket—small, woven, not a statement logo
Wear pattern potential: soft fading at collar edges and cuffs with age, maintaining integrity
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 aspirational—signals economic stability and aesthetic sophistication without corporate excess. Accessible to working creatives, academics, and mid-level professionals who value durability and design heritage over status symbols.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearer is someone who thinks about their choices—a junior architect defending a design concept, an academic attending departmental meetings, a creative director who doesn't need logos to prove capability. Suggests connection to old Chicago craft traditions (Wicker Park lineage) and skepticism toward disposable fast-fashion. Reads as anti-corpo aesthetic even when worn in corporate contexts.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and cared-for. A new Kellstrom & Vane coat shows crisp fold lines and perfect edges; after six months of regular wear, the shoulders settle, the houndstooth gains subtle shine in high-friction areas, edges soften naturally. Owners tend to maintain these pieces—a tailor's visit, occasional pressing, spot-cleaning. The fabric is meant to age gracefully.
